subject: Sprint slot advocacy for Cobalt Systems — requested tradeoffs and timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint slot advocacy for Cobalt Systems — requested tradeoffs and timeline

Team —

Quick context: Cobalt Systems (large fintech prospect) sent a signed LOI this morning committing to a pilot with $425k ARR if we can guarantee deterministic inference performance during their end-of-quarter load windows. The engineering ask driving the commitment is a small, well-scoped runtime feature they call "scheduled residency snapshots": a server-side capability that pins a customer’s model weight/cache residency for pre-specified time windows and emits a compact snapshot artifact that ensures repeatable cold-start behavior for the duration of their billing periods.

Why this matters now:
- Commercial: LOI signed, procurement wants contract language that references "scheduled residency snapshot capability" in the SOW; deal moves to legal tomorrow if we confirm timeline.
- Technical: This is primarily an orchestration + runtime switch with a small persistent snapshot artifact (no new model training).
- Risk/Impact: If we prioritize, we can ship an MVP (API + server-side snapshot orchestration + basic validation checks) in a single sprint with engineering support; the tradeoff is delaying the optional admin UI, deferring long-tail telemetry analytics, and limited backward-compat compatibility testing across quantized variants.

Ask: Can Eng/Product commit a sprint slot in the next Q3 sprint (starts Jun 28) to deliver an MVP limited to:
1) Server-side snapshot orchestration and API surface for reserving snapshot windows
2) Runtime hooks to load snapshot artifacts deterministically for the window
3) A minimal test harness and rollback plan

If we can get a go/no-go by EOD tomorrow (Fri Jun 11), Sales will lock the commercial language and start procurement cadence. Attachments: Cobalt_LOI.pdf, Cobalt_requirements_v1.xlsx.

Recommended tradeoffs if capacity is tight:
- Defer admin UI and dashboarding to post-MVP sprint
- Limit supported model formats initially (float32 only; defer 8-bit/quantization compatibility)
- Ops-runbook required for initial rollout (manual ops steps acceptable for MVP)

Irene/Aditya — can you evaluate feasibility and propose a trimmed acceptance criteria back to me by EOD? Ben/Marissa I’ll coordinate customer expectations while we confirm scope.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint slot advocacy for Cobalt Systems — requested tradeoffs and timeline

Thanks for the context; appreciate the urgency. A few clarifying questions so Product can scope an MVP properly: 

1) Acceptance criteria: What are the exact SLAs Cobalt needs during their windows (p50/p95 latency, throughput guarantees)? The LOI references "deterministic performance" but that needs quantification for tests.
2) Snapshot size and format: Are we expecting full KV cache + tokenizer state, or a narrower artifact? The size will affect storage/cost and snapshot load time.
3) Compatibility: You mentioned deferring 8-bit variants — will Cobalt accept float32-only for MVP?
4) Rollback: Do we want a feature-flagged rollout (canary) or quick manual rollback? Canary would need tracing/traceid hooks in the runtime (we currently have partial support tracked in RED-5310).
5) Test harness: Is Cobalt able to run acceptance tests on their side, or do we need to simulate peak windows in-house?

Operational ask: please add a brief note in the attached requirements spreadsheet that quantifies expected peak tokens/sec and target latency percentiles. That will let Eng estimate risk.

I can draft a trimmed product acceptance criteria doc but need the points above. If Sales confirms SLA numbers and agrees to the proposed tradeoffs (no UI, float32-only), Product can provisionally commit a single sprint scope and we’ll coordinate with Eng.

Irene
Irene Choi
VP Product — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint slot advocacy for Cobalt Systems — requested tradeoffs and timeline

Quick note from the commercial side: Cobalt has indicated this feature is a gating item for the initial purchase order and they are prepared to sign a 12-month commitment with a 20% ARR uplift if we can deliver the MVP in the next 6 weeks. Procurement is flexible on acceptance testing but legal is explicitly asking for the capability to be present in the product by milestone 1 to avoid a credit-triggered SLA clause.

If Product/Eng can commit to the limited-scope MVP (float32-only, no UI) and provide an ops-runbook, Sales will:
- Put the milestone language into the SOW as "scheduled residency snapshot capability (MVP)"
- Agree to a pilot cutover window aligned to our proposed timeline

Commercial downside if we miss the sprint: procurement will push the milestone to the next quarter and the competitive pressure will increase (they are evaluating two alternatives).

Ben
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 02:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sprint slot advocacy for Cobalt Systems — requested tradeoffs and timeline

On Thu, 10 Jun 2027 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick context: Cobalt Systems (large fintech prospect) sent a signed LOI this morning committing to a pilot with $425k ARR if we can guarantee deterministic inference performance during their end-of-quarter load windows. The engineering ask driving the commitment is a small, well-scoped runtime feature they call "scheduled residency snapshots": a server-side capability that pins a customer’s model weight/cache residency for pre-specified time windows and emits a compact snapshot artifact that ensures repeatable cold-start behavior for the duration of their billing periods.

Thanks for the heads-up — we dug into RED-5421 and looked at what an MVP would look like. High-level feasibility statement: we can take a narrowly scoped MVP in the first Q3 sprint but with explicit tradeoffs. Proposed Eng plan (high level):

Scope (MVP — single sprint):
- Scheduler + API for creating snapshot windows (framework-level endpoints)
- Snapshot write/read logic that persists a compact artifact (tokenizer state + KV cache pointers) to S3-compatible storage
- Runtime toggle to deterministically load the snapshot during the reserved window
- Basic integration tests simulating a single peak window and a smoke regression run

Tradeoffs we require:
- Float32-only for MVP (no quantized path)
- No admin UI or long-term dashboarding in sprint; an ops-runbook will be provided for manual control
- Limited cross-compat acceptance testing (we will test a representative model family only)
- Rollout behind a feature flag; initial enablement will be manual via ops-runbook

Estimate: 3 engineers at 80% allocation across the sprint + 1 SRE for manual rollout support. We can deliver the API + runtime hooks + test harness in the sprint start date you suggested, but we need Product to firm up acceptance criteria (latency p95 target) and Sales to add the minimal test dataset to the requirements sheet.

Next steps I propose now:
1) Irene — if Product can draft a concise acceptance criteria doc today, attach to RED-5421.
2) Ben/Soojin — confirm in writing that Sales will accept the MVP tradeoffs (float32-only, no UI, manual ops-runbook) in the SOW.
3) Eng will schedule the sprint nomination and block the nominal headcount today; final go/no-go by close of business Friday Jun 11.

I attached a short design stub: residency-design-proposal.md that captures the storage layout and snapshot lifecycle we plan to use.

Aditya Rao
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
